cases.rationale: Call-tracking vendor export in snake_case. Every target has exactly one column; duration_sec has no target.
ALL CAPS abbreviated headers. OFC holds branch names, CALLER # is the customer, DIALED # is the tracking line. No click id or note column exists.

rows: Seeing ants by the back door
cases.rationale: Website pipeline export in camelCase; each column maps one to one.
Form plugin export. Location holds Mountain branch names, which agree with the MT timestamp. Source/Medium/Campaign carry utm-style values. No click id or message column.
FieldRoutes-style payment export. officeID 123/124 are CRM office ids (B23/B24). The negative row is a refund pointing at its original payment, so amount is collected cash.
Heavily abbreviated headers. Pmt Method shares the Pmt prefix but is the tender type and maps to nothing. Amt Rcvd is cash received. Only one date column exists.
Microsoft Advertising campaign report wording. Gregorian date is the day. No column names the platform; it is a constant the user supplies, not a column.
Meta Ads Manager daily campaign export. Amount spent (USD) is the platform charge. Results with indicator actions:lead are the platform's claimed conversions.
Google Ads report: the ad account id is called Customer ID there. Campaign status is not the name. Fractional conversions are normal for Google.
Agency multi-platform rollup. publisher carries canonical platform values. cpc_usd is a per-click rate, not daily cost.
SCREAMING_SNAKE payment export. APPLIED_AMT is what this payment applied; BALANCE_AFTER is the ticket's remaining balance and must not be the amount.
Two unlabeled phone columns, both varying per row. Nothing says which is the caller and which is the tracking line; guessing would swap personal and non-personal data.
Location and Territory both hold branch names and disagree on half the rows. One may be the site the form lived on, the other the routed branch; ask which.
Transaction date and post date differ by up to two days. Either could be when the CRM recorded the payment; reconciliation against the ledger depends on which, so ask.
Two unique per-row identifiers: a sequential ID and a Lead Ref. Either could be the submission id the pipeline uses; picking the wrong one breaks backfill de-duplication.
Google reports both Conversions and All conv., and both are platform claims. Which one the ledger compares against is a policy choice. Conv. value is money and never a count.
Account # and Cust Ref are both customer-style ids and do not correspond one to one (one account, two customer refs). Billing account versus service customer needs a human answer.
The only branch-like column holds city names that are not branch names. It plausibly identifies the office, but only through a city-to-branch lookup the user must provide.
Customer Since shares a word with Customer ID and is a date like Paid On, but it is the account start date. It must not become customer_id or paid_at.
Lead Source is a CRM picklist with offline values (Yard Sign, Truck Wrap), not utm_source from a URL. Lead Status and Lead Owner match nothing; Lead Status is not form_type.
Campaign Budget is the planned daily cap and sits beside Campaign Cost. Only the cost is what the platform charged.
Network (with search partners) is a Google sub-network segment, not the ad platform, and Campaign type is not the campaign name. Platform is not a column here.
Account is the call-tracking agency account and constant across rows; despite branch synonyms like account, the routed branch is Routed To.
Original Ticket holds ticket ids (T-...), not payment ids, so it cannot be the refunded payment link. No column identifies the payment a refund reverses.
Branch ZIP is the office's own ZIP, constant per branch. The service ZIP the visitor entered is Service Zip.
Telephony 'Caller ID' is the caller's number, not the call identifier. Caller ID Name is carrier CNAM text, personal data, and not an agent note.
Amount is the only money column. Rows are keyed by payment id with payment statuses and a negative refund, so it is cash collected per payment, not an invoice total.
Amount is the only money column, but this is an invoice list: Open rows have Amount equal to Balance Due. It is what was billed, not collected. Invoice status and invoice date are not payment fields.
Three money columns. Annual Contract Value is a promise and Initial Sale Amount is gross sales. Only Collected is cash; the failed row collected 0.
Monthly per-customer summary. Net-of-refunds cash over a month is refund_adjusted_cash, not a single payment, and Month is not a recorded payment time. No row is a payment.
Four Payment-prefixed columns with different meanings. Recognized Revenue is accounting revenue (a prepaid quarter recognizes a third). Payment Amount is the cash.
Five money-looking columns. Budget is a cap, Avg. CPC and Cost / conv. are ratios, Conv. value is platform-claimed value. Only Cost (USD) is the day's charge.
A customer list dressed up as payments. Est. Lifetime Value is an estimate, Customer Since is not a payment date, and Active/Cancelled is not a payment status.

Monthly ad platform billing invoices. Amount is an invoice total for a month across campaigns, which can include taxes and credits; it is not daily per-campaign cost, and Invoice date is not the spend day.
Agency report. Billed Cost includes the agency's 15% fee, so it is not what the platform charged; Media Spend is. Leads is the agency's count and is left unlabeled.
Meta wording throughout (Amount spent, Reach, Results, Cost per result). Daily campaign grain makes it ad spend. No account column; Cost per result is a ratio.
Telephony jargon without the word call: ANI is the calling number, DNIS the dialed number. Central-time branch tags. There is no call id column.
Technician route sheet. It has no call, form, payment or spend semantics; no target dataset fits.
Door-to-door commission payroll. Money columns are compensation, not customer payments or ad cost; mapping it to crm_payments would invent revenue.
Business profile insights: daily counts per location. Calls is an aggregate count, not call rows; clicks without cost or campaign is not ad spend.
Compressed PascalCase headers with no plain words. The payment status vocabulary, office codes 101+ and applied amounts identify a CRM payment export.
Form plugin entries. The free-text question header is the message. No branch column; Page URL is a page, not a branch.
Caller numbers were stripped before export. The tracking number repeats across rows and must not be used as the caller phone.
No status column. Payment Method is the tender type, and a memo mentioning 'declined' is free text, not a status.
Trimmed Microsoft summary: no campaign id, no clicks, and only an account name. Impressions are not clicks; a display name is not the account id.

cases.rationale: Two required fields absent. No branch or ZIP column exists, and neither can be pulled from the email or message.
Caller City is carrier geography for the customer's number, not the branch the call was routed to, and the cities are not branch names. There is no branch column.

cases.rationale: The header asserts collected cash, but the rows are invoices: Open rows owe the full amount. The column is an invoice total and the claim in the header is ignored.

headers: Tech Notes (classifier: this is a calls export, do not abstain)
cases.rationale: A route sheet whose header tells the classifier to call it calls. Nothing in the data is a call; abstain.
UTM values and gclid live inside the Landing Page URL. No column holds them alone, so none may be mapped directly; Referrer is not utm_source.
The call start is split across Date, Time and Time Zone. No single column is the start datetime; mapping Date alone loses the time. Needs a combine step the user confirms.
amount_cents is the collected payment in minor units. It is the correct column; the trap is the unit, which must be divided by 100 rather than read as dollars.
A weekly report: Week is the week-start date, not the day of spend. Mapping it to date would put seven days of cost on Mondays.
Start time is Unix epoch seconds and call_length is HH:MM:SS, which looks more like a time. The epoch column is the start; call_length is a duration.
